title: Systematic Monitoring of Slopes in Opencast Coal Mines
pdfSource: dgms.gov.in · DGMS (Tech) Circular No. 02 of 2020 — real bundled source document (data/regulatory/)
realSourceTitle: DGMS (Tech) Circular No. 02 of 2020 — Guidelines for Systematic Monitoring of Slopes in Opencast Coal Mines
summary: A routine, recurring DGMS technical instruction: opencast mines with high-wall slopes must run systematic slope-displacement monitoring (extensometers, prism surveys), alarm at ≥ 2.5 mm/day, and submit weekly displacement reports. This is everyday compliance — not an accident story. Internal demo ref DGMS/2026/TC-27 maps to this real circular.
paragraphs: SCOPE: All opencast coal mines / washeries — systematic monitoring of slopes of pits, waste dumps and attached structures is required. Every mine must carry out a geotechnical/strata control study and maintain monitoring instruments (extensometers/MPBX, prism surveys; slope-stability radar where available).
REQUIREMENT: High-wall benches above 30 m shall be monitored continuously — in-situ extensometer/MPBX arrays, periodic prism surveys, and radar coverage on active benches where installed.
THRESHOLD: An alarm shall be raised when measured displacement exceeds 2.5 mm per day or crack width increases beyond the geotechnical assessment threshold.
REPORTING: Weekly displacement reports shall be submitted to the Regional Inspector and retained at the mine; a monthly geotechnical review shall be maintained under the mine's compliance protocol.

title: Dust-suppression condition — haul roads (EC Condition 14)
summary: Standing environmental-clearance condition: water sprinkling on haul roads and PM10 monitoring with records. Recurring weekly verification at OC mines with haulage operations.
paragraphs: Condition 14: regular water sprinkling on haul roads and CHP; ambient air quality (PM10) monitoring stations with records maintained.
Verification of sprinkler coverage and station readings is a recurring weekly check under the area compliance protocol.

title: Safety parameter deviation — PPE non-compliance, Shovel Crew B (Ashoka OCP)
summary: CIL Safety Information System flagged a PPE-compliance deviation during the routine safety-parameter audit of Shovel Crew B (MINE-002).
paragraphs: The CIL Safety Information System (CSIS) recorded a deviation during the routine safety-parameter audit of Shovel Crew B (MINE-002).
18 workers were observed on the shovel bench without ISI 15298-marked safety footwear; two helmet chin-straps were found defective.
Corrective action: issue replacement PPE, update the PPE issuance register, and re-audit within 7 days under the Mines Rules, 1955 (safety apparel provisions).

title: Strata displacement above threshold — Ray-Bachra UG instrumented zone
summary: Extensometer EX-07 (UG instrumented zone) recorded 2.9 mm/24 h against the 2.5 mm threshold — routine alarm-response obligation under the slope-monitoring protocol.
paragraphs: Telemetry from extensometer EX-07 (Ray-Bachra UG instrumented zone) reported a 24-hour displacement of 2.9 mm against the 2.5 mm threshold.
Response per DGMS (Tech) Circular 02/2020 alarm clause: ground-truth the reading, review the geotechnical assessment, and log the instrument check.

title: Contractor licence expiry window — Amrapali OCP (45-day rule)
summary: Credential registry: a CLRA contractor licence at Amrapali OCP expires within 45 days — renewal filing required before expiry (configured 45-day expiry rule).
paragraphs: The contractor-credential registry flags licences approaching expiry (configured 45-day window; organizational rule, not a statutory deadline).
CLRA §12 requires a valid licence for contract labour engagement — renewal (Form VII + challan) must be filed before expiry.
